prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production 2D game animation sprite sheet for Moss Circuit, transparent PNG, sixteen animation frames in a strict four-column by four-row grid, row-major time order.
Primary request: Create the Warden robot's STRAIGHT FORWARD SHOULDER CHARGE action, distinctly different from its existing double-fist ground slam. Use the reference only for the exact robot identity and art style.
Input image 1: reference image for identity/style, not an edit target. Keep the moss-covered squat olive-and-rust armored robot, off-white small rectangular face plate, narrow amber eyes, two massive asymmetric stone-metal fists, short heavy legs, small vertical rear exhaust. Three-quarter view facing LEFT throughout.
Style/medium: crisp detailed game sprite, chunky pixel-art-inspired edges, exactly the same material palette and body proportions as the reference. NO environment or shadows on a floor. Pure transparent empty background, genuine alpha.
Composition/framing: exactly 16 cells in a 4 by 4 sheet, equal square cells; one full robot per cell, generous clear gutters. Robot feet rest on an identical low baseline within every cell. Entire robot and effects fully inside its cell. Same camera, same character scale in every frame. No text or labels.
Sequence in row-major time order:
frames 0-5 preparation: neutral stance, short knees bend, left-leading shoulder drops, both heavy fists tuck in close as a ram shield, progressively stronger low forward lean; feet remain planted. NO raised-overhead fists.
frames 6-11 active charge: forward-leaning shoulder ram LEFT with fists tucked, clearly alternating running legs and body compression/extension; mechanical identity intact. Small attached backward dust flecks allowed, no large speed streaks, no detached projectiles.
frames 12-15 recovery: heel braking, torso rises, fists lower, settle into reference neutral stance.
Constraints: no ground slam, no shockwave, no orange impact star, no clone overlays, no duplicate poses across all sixteen, no black/white/checkerboard background, no vignette, no diffuse glow halo, no ground, no arbitrary size changes. Retain all robot parts and visual identity. The final pose must be upright alive, not a hurt or death pose.
Make the silhouette change unmistakable so a player can read charge vs slam at small scale.
